summary: Revise at 6.0. Caiman scores 7 and the ship bar is 7.5. Every gate recorded in report.json is green at draft (768x320) and at export (1536x448). The template gate has not been run and is not recorded, so it is still open. The idea reads. At 300 px, uncaptioned, a dark thorny branch with five-petal white-gold blossoms and a blue-black round fruit says flowering blackthorn or plum within a second or two, and the diagonal twig across the 013 table gives a silhouette of its own. The execution is round-1 work. (1) The 'calyx' still reads as a six-claw mechanical crown, which read test 6 already flagged and this round did not fix. In face.png, hero.png and stones.png it is five flat-topped, square-cut, darkened blocks plus a straight rod for the stalk. The sloe sits in a turned dish cut into the table, so it does not hang from the twig. (2) The twig is not one continuous sculpted branch. In stones.png and face.png it is broken by flat-ended gold collar cylinders at the spur and blossom roots, around nodes 0-2, 4-6 and 8-9. Its bark is smeared and noisy rather than furrowed. The petals show combed and stair-stepped edges with pin-like stamen spikes. (3) The ornament covers roughly a quarter of the ring. The twig lies on one cheek of the head only, and the opposite cheek, both shank walls, the shoulders behind the head and the whole palm (palm.png, reverse.png) are bare polished factory stock. That fails one-theme-face-to-palm and density against Caiman and the Reptilia sheet. (4) The spurs are smooth straight cones with no root flare or curve. They read as hardware spikes, not blackthorn spurs. One more finding: the export's sampled section diagnostic records 4307 vertices under 0.8 mm (least 0.012 mm at [8.94, 9.41, 1.38], beside blossom 9 and spur 8). The author answers it with sections by construction, and the field's thinnest wall is 1.40 mm, but it has to be resolved or explained, not just carried. A concrete round can close all of this: rebuild the calyx and stalk, continue the twig round the shank to the palm, remove the collars and fair the bark.
strengths: Reads as its plant at 300 px: a thorned dark branch, five-petal blossoms and a dusky round fruit point to blackthorn or sloe without the caption (hero-300, face-300).
The silhouette is distinctive. The diagonal twig crosses the 013 table, and its spurs break the outline on both sides in face and side views.
Colour hierarchy: dark bark, bright gold blossoms and a blue-black onyx (matching the sloe's bloom) give three clear values.
The blossoms are true five-petal parts with real relief. The two 3.9 mm blossoms at nodes 3 and 5 read cleanly at 300 px.
Graded spurs (2.1-4.0 mm) with alternating turn give the twig rhythm.
Gates are clean: watertight, 0 degenerate, 0 self-crossings on the ring and 20 made parts, Castable under lost wax, 0 DFM, 1 = 1 stone, cold reload identical, 1.27 M triangles at export.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: Nothing is scattered, but the theme stops at the head. palm.png and reverse.png show bare factory stock across the whole palm, the far cheek and both rear shank walls. The planned Straif mark is absent, and there is no bark or twig behind theta of about +/-60 deg.

checklist.item: Reads as its plant at 300 px without the caption
checklist.reason: hero-300 and face-300 read as a flowering thorny branch with a dark fruit (blackthorn or plum). The crown-like stone mount is the one element that argues against the read.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: stones.png shows combed vertical striations on the petal sides (blossoms at nodes 3 and 5), stair-stepped edges on the gold collars, pin-spike stamens, and a smeared, streaky bark surface with no legible furrows.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, visible, coloured as fruit or buds
checklist.reason: The onyx is visible and its blue-black is right for a sloe, but the made setting reads as a mechanical six-claw crown: five flat-topped rectangular sepal blocks and a straight rod stalk, darkened like recesses. It is not a calyx, and the fruit sits in a dish cut into the table instead of hanging from the twig.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms are sculpted
checklist.reason: Sepals are square-cut blocks. The twig carries flat-ended cylindrical collars at every spur and blossom root. The spurs are plain straight cones with a hard joint to the collar.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: The 013 walls and table edge are intact where unornamented (bare-vs-finished.png). The ragged line at the table rim is present on the bare stock too.

checklist.item: Silhouette distinct from the other Vepres rings
checklist.reason: No other Vepres ring is built yet. A diagonal thorned branch over a round signet with protruding spurs is unlike the planned cane, ivy and holly silhouettes.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: Large (sloe), medium (twig, spurs) and small (blossoms) forms are present, but on about 25% of the surface. Caiman and the Reptilia signets carry ornament over the whole head and shank, and here the shank and palm are blank.

gates.verified: draft and export blocks: watertight true, degenerate_faces 0, boundary_edges 0, non_manifold_edges 0; casting_pattern watertight, 0 degenerate

gates.gate: 0 self-crossings on the ring and every made part
gates.verified: ring_self_crossings 0, made_part_crossings_worst 0, made_parts_crossing [] over 20 made parts, both builds
solids_notes [] and parts_notes [] in both builds
bore_clear true; closest vertex 8.568 mm vs bore radius 8.578 mm (0.01 mm, which is the bore surface itself)
field_verdict 'Castable' under process 'Lost wax' in draft and export; not 'with care'

gates.gate: Lost wax thinnest wall >= 0.8 mm (replaces ray release and clamp)
gates.verified: thinnest_wall_mm 1.4046 and sections_ok true in both builds. Caveat: section_sampled_diagnostic records 4307 of 90641 vertices under 0.8 mm, least 0.012 mm at [8.94, 9.41, 1.38], which the JSON does not explain (see punch item 6)

gates.gate: Stone count equals preview; no metal in stones
gates.verified: stones_reported 1, stones_previewed 1; metal_inside_stones 0 vertices; stones.json lists one onyx; crowding []
casting_pattern: watertight, 0 degenerate, 0 self-crossings, pass true

gates.gate: Template gate (<= 4 design.set patches, class budget)
gates.verified: not recorded in report.json; design_bytes 1,131,225, over the 1 MB stock budget

punch_list.zone: Sloe mount: 'Calyx cup', 'Calyx sepal 1-5', 'Sloe stalk' at sloe centre xz (-0.3, -2.2)
punch_list.change: Replace the five rectangular sepal blocks with five lofted, pointed, slightly reflexed sepals that wrap the fruit's lower third. Each should be ovate (about 1.6 mm long x 1.1 mm wide at the base), tapering to a 0.38 mm tip, with a rounded section and no flat top or square end. Keep every sepal tip below the stone's equator. Fill the turned dish in the table level with the table, and lift the sloe on a curved stalk, at least 1.5 mm long and 0.9-1.2 mm thick, that rises out of the twig (node 4 or 5) so the fruit visibly hangs from the branch. Render the sepals in bright gold, not recess-dark.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and stones.png no sepal shows a flat top face or a square corner, and no sepal rises above the stone's equator. In hero-300 an uncaptioned viewer sees a fruit on a stalk from the twig, not a claw or crown head. The table shows no sunken dish around the stone.

punch_list.zone: Twig over the head, all node collars (roots of spurs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 and blossoms 1, 3, 5, 7, 9)
punch_list.change: Remove the flat-ended cylindrical collars. Blend each spur and blossom root into the twig with a 0.3-0.5 mm fillet or a swollen node bud that flows into the bark, so the wood is one continuous tapering sweep (about 1.5:1 from the head outward). Rebuild the bark as 3-5 longitudinal fissures, 0.15-0.25 mm deep and following the sweep, plus scattered lenticel dashes, in place of the current smeared noise.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png and face.png no collar shows a flat end face or a stepped edge, and the gold-on-dark banding at the nodes is gone. Bark fissures read as continuous lines along the twig at 1600 px.

punch_list.zone: Shank walls and palm: theta from about +/-60 deg to 180 deg on both sides, and the far cheek of the head
punch_list.change: Carry the plant face to palm. Run the twig (or a second, thinner shoot, 0.8-1.0 mm radius) from each end of the head twig down both shank walls to the palm. Give it 3-4 smaller spurs a side (1.2-2.0 mm) and 1-2 small blossoms or buds (2.4-2.8 mm) per side. Put the Straif Ogham bench-cut on the palm crest (6 mm stem, five 1.6 x 0.35 mm diagonal strokes). Add shallow bark furrows (0.25-0.35 mm) on the walls under the twig, so no wall reads as bare polished stock.
punch_list.acceptance: palm.png and reverse.png show the twig or shoot and the Straif mark, and no area larger than one 10 mm x 4 mm patch of bare factory polish remains outside the bore and the table rim. In side.png the branch is seen continuing round the band.

punch_list.zone: Spurs 0, 2, 4, 6, 8 on the twig over the head
punch_list.change: Sculpt the spurs as blackthorn spurs, not cones. Flare each root into the wood over about 0.8 mm, give each a slight curve (sagitta 0.15-0.3 mm over its length) and a faintly faceted or ridged section, and keep the 0.1 mm point. Retain the graded lengths.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and hero.png each spur shows a visible root swell and a curved axis, and none reads as a straight machined cone on a cylinder.

punch_list.change: Clean the petal geometry: no vertical combing on petal sides, and smooth cupped petals with a 0.15-0.2 mm recessed gap between them. Replace the pin-spike stamens with 8-12 short rounded stamen beads (0.15-0.2 mm) round a domed heart. Raise the two 3.2 mm blossoms at nodes 7 and 9 to at least 3.6 mm, or drop one of them, so all blossoms sit clear of the twig.
punch_list.acceptance: In stones.png the petal sides are smooth with no striations, and no stamen reads as a needle. In face-300 each blossom shows five separate petals.

punch_list.zone: Finished mesh near [8.94, 9.41, 1.38] (blossom 9, spur 8, twig end) and report.json
punch_list.change: Resolve the section_sampled_diagnostic: 4307 vertices under 0.8 mm, least 0.012 mm. Either thicken the thin flap (a likely blossom margin or seam pad standing off the band), or add to report.json a per-cluster breakdown showing that each cluster below 0.8 mm is a petal or sepal margin, a point, or a ray artefact, with its location.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json's section_sampled_diagnostic either has least_mm >= 0.8 outside listed points, or carries a cluster list in which every entry is explained. thinnest_wall_mm stays >= 0.8.

punch_list.change: Run the template gate and record it: lift evaluates cold byte-identical, at most 4 design.set patches, size and open time in verification.json. Bring design_bytes (1.13 MB) under the 1 MB stock budget, or record the overage with its cause.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json or verification.json records template pass with a patch count <= 4 and its byte size within the class budget.
